> **Generated — do not hand-edit this table.** Each row's source is
> `_registry/<CR###>.row.md` (one file per CR); rebuild with
> `scripts/registers/gen_registers.py gen cr`. See [How a CR works](#how-a-cr-works).

The register of **planned change** — new work, not fixes. A CR is anything that adds or
changes behaviour versus the current build: a feature, a refactor, a process change, a
content or infra change. (Fixing something already broken is a **Defect** —
see [`../defect/def_list.md`](../defect/def_list.md).)

Governance rationale: decision **D-058** in [`../initial_specs/11_decisions/decision_log.md`](../initial_specs/11_decisions/decision_log.md).

## How a CR works

- **This table is generated — never hand-edit it.** Each row's source is
  `_registry/CR###.row.md` (one file per CR = a disjoint write-path); rebuild with
  `python scripts/registers/gen_registers.py gen cr`. A shared monolithic table gets *swept*
  on the shared `main` checkout ([CR081](CR081_registers_are_architect_write_only/CR081_registers_are_architect_write_only.md));
  one-file-per-item removes the shared write entirely.
- **Auto-file, proceed.** Saiful's prompt IS the approval. When he asks for a change, the
  **Architect mints the next `CR###`** (one minter, no ID-collision race); its **domain
  owner** writes `_registry/CR###.row.md` + creates the folder + files the CR doc, then
  implements — no separate approval gate. A web CR's row is written by `coder.web`, a backend
  CR's by `coder.api`, etc. — the register is no longer an Architect chokepoint (it only mints
  the number, which is domain-agnostic).
- **ID:** `CR###`, zero-padded, sequential, never reused.
- **Folder:** every CR gets `docs/forward_planning/CR###_<snake_case_topic>/`. It holds at
  minimum `CR###_<topic>.md` (what / why / scope / acceptance). All design docs, notes, and
  sub-specs for that change live in its folder.
- **Regenerate + pathspec-commit:** after writing/editing a row file, run the generator and
  `git commit -m "…" -- <your row file> docs/forward_planning/cr_list.md`. Never bare /
  `-am` / `git add -A`.
- **Commit tag:** the fix/feat commit carries `(AT:R<N> CR###)` after the summary, e.g.
  `feat(journal): search across entries (AT:R42 CR007)`.
- **Exempt from needing a CR:** process commits — handover wraps (`chore(handover)`),
  TestFlight/build version bumps, and docs-only commits. These keep the plain `(AT:R<N>)` tag.

**Status:** `proposed` · `in_progress` · `done` · `dropped`.

| CR075 | 2026-07-23 | **Download the Sharia universe once a day and hold it.** Saiful: *"Why don't we download and hold it for other users? We can do the download every day."* Today the universe lives only in **process memory** — each container builds its own copy on first use, re-fetched no more often than every 900 s — so network sits on the request path (the first halal trade after a restart pays for the fetch), every restart re-downloads, two workers can hold two different as-of dates, and **a source outage of any length means `UNAVAILABLE` ⇒ every halal-flagged trade blocked** ([DEF093](../defect/DEF093_disabled_flag_blocks_every_halal_trade/)'s blast radius triggered by a bad minute on a host we don't control). For a filter a user turned on for religious reasons, *"we couldn't reach a CSV, so you may not trade"* is a poor answer when yesterday's list was fine and the standard itself only changes at rebalance. **It also closes the freshness gap nothing else could:** the parent-index mirror publishes no as-of of its own, so SPUS's date is currently the only staleness signal and a frozen parent list would go unnoticed — a stored row carries **`fetched_at`**, stamped by us, which *is* the missing signal. And it makes the claim defensible: constraint 1 requires naming standard + source + as-of wherever a verdict shows, and holding the list makes that date a fact we recorded rather than a property of whatever we happened to fetch — if anyone asks which companies AMI treated as compliant on a given day, a row answers it. **Design:** a small `coder.api`-owned table (standard, source URL, file `as_of`, our `fetched_at`, compliant set, parent set — two lists of a few hundred tickers, size is a non-issue); refresh via a background task in the **existing** pattern (`main.py` already runs `_nightly_audit_trim()` and `_league_roll_tick()` as startup asyncio tasks — **no new dependency, no new mechanism**), with a tick that finds a fresh row doing nothing so restarts can't miss a boundary; read path resolves from the row, so no network, no `asyncio.to_thread`, no first-request stall, and the in-process cache becomes a read-through rather than the source of truth. **Unchanged:** no failover/union/intersection (one named primary standard, §3a — holding one standard's list is not blending two); `sharia_screen()` stays dormant (constraint 4); blocking on genuine staleness stays (constraint 3 — this only buys a longer runway before it fires); G3 unknown-permits unchanged. **Open for the build lane:** whether a *held* list should be servable longer than a *fetched* one (stated, not inherited); first-boot seeding with an empty table and an unreachable source is still correctly `UNAVAILABLE`; and a refresh failing three days running while the list is still in-window must be visible to **us** even though it's invisible to the user — degrade-loudly applied to the refresher, not the reader. `GATE: independent` recorded upfront — it changes what an observance filter enforces and how it fails, and it touches the schema. | proposed | [CR075_persist_the_sharia_universe/](CR075_persist_the_sharia_universe/) | AT:architect |

| CR077 | 2026-07-23 | **Prompt caching is already on, delivers 0% on Room prompts, and could not have helped much anyway.** Saiful: *"lots of our messages to the llm are static, especially for the agents. is there a way we can speed up the processing by pre-caching a major part of the prompt?"* The premise is right; the conclusion doesn't follow. **Measured on the live serving host** (`192.168.20.74:8000`, vLLM `0.23.1.dev0`, `ami-llm` = `RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4`): prefix caching is **already enabled** (`enable_prefix_caching="True"`, lifetime 17,151,568/50,924,616 = 33.7% of queried tokens) — nothing to turn on. But `ami-llm` is a **Mamba/attention hybrid**, so vLLM auto-resolves `block_size` up to **2,096 tokens** to align the Mamba and attention pages, and caching is whole-block only. **Measured cliff: a 2,095-token prompt repeated verbatim reuses 0 tokens; 2,096 reuses a full block** — and every reuse observed was a multiple of 2,096 (2096/4192/6288/14672). Every Room agent system prompt is **1,143–2,264 tokens** (the static base+overlay part only 635–1,387), so the Room gets **exactly zero** cache benefit today; the 33.7% comes from elsewhere. Known upstream issue, not our misconfiguration — vllm-project/vllm #40696. The twelve agents also share **no** common prefix: `build_agent_prompt()` puts `content/agents/<id>.md` at token 0, so they diverge on the first token. **And fixing it wouldn't matter: prefill is ~4% of a turn.** Decode measured at **33.0 tok/s** single-stream (200 tok in 6.07 s, 400 in 11.89 s — same rate); prefilling a whole 1,300-token prompt costs **0.29 s** against **~7.6 s** to generate a 250-token turn. Perfect caching of 100% of every prompt cuts a convene ~4%. **The real lever is concurrency.** Same host, `min_tokens` forced, streams salted against cache cross-talk: 1→33.0 tok/s, 2→57.1 (1.73×), 4→91.1 (**2.77×**), 8→150.5 (**4.57×**) aggregate; and the card is at `gpu_memory_utilization=0.5` with 3.49M tokens of KV cache — half unused. `room_runner.py:1375-1393` runs all twelve agents strictly sequentially. Exactly one phase could change: **ANALYSTS** (fundamentals/market/news/social, four independent domains) — ~4×6.1 s becomes ~8.8 s, **~15 s off a convene, ~4× what perfect caching could ever deliver**. RESEARCHERS (bear answers bull) and RISK (three debators) must stay sequential — the dependency is the point. **The catch, raised by this lane not discovered later:** every prompt carries `Transcript so far:` and *"build on the transcript — do not repeat what's already been said"* (`room_prompts.py:214,220`), so concurrent analysts go blind to each other and will repeat. That is a **Room-quality** call, decided by reading real output, not by reasoning — hence **Phase 1 is a blocking A/B on 5 tickers, and no code ships before it**; if quality drops the CR closes at a documented "no". Phase 2 parallelises ANALYSTS only, behind a `parallel: bool` on `_Phase` with deterministic `RoomEvent` ordering; Phase 3 raises `gpu_memory_utilization` (ops on the LLM host — this workstation has no SSH to it). **Explicitly refused:** restructuring prompts to build a ≥2,096-token shared prefix. It moves the per-agent persona to the *end*, colliding with the safety-floor ordering rule (`agent_prompts.py:64-65` — the floor is appended last *so it dominates*) and CR038's ~70% instruction-compliance finding. Room-quality risk of that size for 4% of wall clock is a bad trade; revisit only if upstream lands sub-block caching. **Silent-failure trap recorded** for whoever does: in `align` cache mode (ours), if the Mamba checkpoint lands in request-unique tokens vLLM discards the *entire* prefix match including perfectly-matched attention blocks, and the hit rate drops to zero with no signal — vllm-project/vllm #45238. CR040's degrade-loudly class arriving from inside the inference server; hence the second guard, **log the measured hit rate at startup** — nobody would currently notice if caching were off. First guard: a test asserting the phases marked parallel are exactly the phases whose agents don't read each other — someone later marking RISK parallel would silently delete the risk debate while every test passes and the UI still renders three contributions, which is DEF084's shape. Also flagged in passing: CLAUDE.md's runtime table still says the LLM is *"Gemma 4 31B"*; the host reports **Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4**. Brief — architect/build team implements; this lane files and reviews.  **AMENDED same day — Saiful: *"concierge take 20K token"*, and that flips the answer for one surface.** The Concierge system prompt measures **15,731 tokens**, of which **14,558 is the lesson catalogue** — `_full_context_index()` rendering all **342** lessons (`concierge_prompts.py:317`, CR020 `full_context`), **byte-identical for every user** and changing only when a lesson is added. A prefix cache matches from token 0 and stops at the first difference, so one differing mandate field invalidates all 14,558 tokens behind it; the cacheable prefix is `base` alone at **892 tokens — under the 2,096 cliff, so zero**. **Measured A/B against the live cache, two users differing only in mandate:** current order → 2nd user gets **0 cached, 2,672 ms**; catalogue-first → 2nd user gets **14,672 cached, 344 ms**. **7.8×, 2.33 s saved per message**, for the cost of moving one block earlier in an f-string. **Not oversold:** within one conversation the system prompt is already identical turn-to-turn, so today's shape already caches from turn 2 (measured same-user: 2,674 → 389 → 391 ms). The reorder buys **the first message of every conversation for every user after the first** — the message users actually notice. **Second-order win, arguably bigger:** today each user needs a private 15.7K-token KV copy (~222 concurrent contexts fit in the 3.49M-token cache, evicting Room traffic when they don't); shared-prefix, all users draw on **one** copy and need ~1K each — ~15× less footprint. **Safe where the Room reorder is not:** the catalogue is *reference data*, not instructions, so moving it reorders no instruction relative to another; the Concierge has no safety floor (PM-only); and the rules referencing it (*"never invent a lesson… name ONLY the lessons in that agent's list above"*) stay last.
